etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in the 1450s, in Middle English; inherited from Middle English obdurat(e), borrowed from Latin obdūrātus (“hardened”), perfect passive participle of obdūrō (“to harden”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from ob- (“against”) + dūrō (“to harden, render hard”), from dūrus (“hard”). Compare durable, endure.
senses: Stubbornly persistent, generally in wrongdoing; refusing to reform or repent.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin obdūrātus, see Etymology 1 and -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more
